summary: Two independent problems were found. The slowness and token-cost alert are most probably caused by an orchestrator agent loop that repeats get_holdings (x38 per session, 195 aborts logged) and multiplies LLM calls per request, starting around 10:55 with flat rps and no llm-gateway change. The blank notifications most probably come from a separate cause: msg-delivery's 11:24 'notification template refactor' deploy, after which renders fail on missing variable 'portfolio_value' from 11:25. The blank notifications began about 30 minutes after the token and latency onset, and msg-delivery logged no render failures before 11:25 (a query that ended at 11:24:59). The trigger for the orchestrator loop is not identified, and the msg-delivery diff is not available, so the template cause rests on timing and log content.

hypotheses.statement: orchestrator enters an agent loop (get_holdings repeated x38 per session, 195 aborts) that multiplies LLM calls per request, driving llm-gateway token usage and orchestrator latency up from 10:55 with flat rps and no llm-gateway fault or change.
hypotheses.label: high

supporting.text: Orchestrator logged an agent loop abort for repeated get_holdings x38 in one session starting 10:55:20Z. 195 abort lines were logged through 11:59:51Z, and the query was complete.

Token usage and orchestrator latency both first deviated in the 10:55 bucket, with tokens later pinned at 400000 and latency roughly doubled to about 2000 ms. llm-gateway usage first exceeded the alert threshold at 10:55:52Z, shortly after the loop began.

Request volume was flat (rps 51.7-58.3), so per-request work rather than traffic is the more likely driver. Orchestrator-to-llm-gateway upstream timeouts began at 10:58:17Z, consistent with extra LLM load. Orchestrator's heaviest dependency is llm-gateway (weight 0.7), making it the main path to token cost.
llm-gateway fallback and parse-failure rates were flat, which argues against a fallback or parse-failure explanation. This points to extra calls rather than a gateway fault.

contradicting.text: The loop's trigger is unexplained. It is an assumption that the loop is generated inside orchestrator because portfolio-svc logged nothing relevant. A prompt or tool-schema change in orchestrator is not ruled out, because the change feed does not track those.
The 400000 tokens_per_min plateau may be a metric ceiling or clamp, so the true peak and cost are unknown. Metric buckets are 5 minutes wide, so the exact onset order within 10:55 cannot be resolved.

hypotheses.statement: msg-delivery's 11:24 'notification template refactor' deploy broke rendering (template needs variable 'portfolio_value' that the payload does not supply), so notifications are sent with empty bodies from 11:25, independent of the slowness and token problem.
hypotheses.label: high

supporting.text: msg-delivery deployed 'notification template refactor' at 11:24:00Z. It was the only msg-delivery change in the window, and the change query was complete.

msg-delivery err_rate jumped from about 0.004 to 0.084 at 11:25. The first render failure on missing variable 'portfolio_value' was logged at 11:25:18Z, and the first 'empty body' warning at 11:26:06Z.
Restarts stayed at 0 and memory stayed in a narrow band, which argues against a crash or memory-pressure explanation.

msg-delivery logged zero render-failure, missing-variable or empty-body lines from 10:55 to 11:24:59, even though the orchestrator loop was already running. This fits failures starting after the deploy rather than with the loop.
It is likely that failed renders are redelivered rather than dropped, based on a manual count of redelivery warnings (approximate).

contradicting.text: The causal link rests on timing and the deploy note alone. The diff is unavailable, so it is unverified whether the refactor made portfolio_value required or whether the orchestrator payload changed.

The zero-match queries ended at 11:24:59, before the first failure, so they cannot test whether the deploy caused the failures. They are also exact-string matches only. It is not checked whether only some payloads lack portfolio_value, and the logs carry no user or message type.
The blank-notification count is not established because the logs are truncated (257 matches, 200 shown).

hypotheses.statement: The orchestrator agent loop aborts before obtaining holdings, so it publishes payloads without portfolio_value to outbound-msgs and msg-delivery fails to render them, linking blank notifications to the token and latency problem rather than the deploy.
hypotheses.label: low

supporting.text: Orchestrator publishes to outbound-msgs, which msg-delivery consumes. In principle incomplete orchestrator payloads could produce render failures downstream.

contradicting.text: Render failures were absent from 10:55 to 11:24:59 while the loop was already aborting, which contradicts the prediction that incomplete payloads would fail rendering from about 10:55.
Orchestrator publish logging is not confirmed, so the absence of portfolio_value or outbound-msgs lines there does not show the payloads were complete.

hypotheses.statement: An upstream trigger such as a prompt or tool-schema change in orchestrator, or a portfolio-svc/redis-cache data issue (cache misses, slowlog), caused get_holdings results to be unusable and started the loop at 10:55.
hypotheses.label: low

supporting.text: A few portfolio-svc holdings cache-miss WARNs (first at 10:32:38Z) and redis-cache slowlog WARNs (first at 10:39:16Z) occurred before the loop. This is only a weak temporal association.

contradicting.text: portfolio-svc latency and error rate were flat, redis-cache latency was flat, and redis-cache evicted_keys stayed at 0. This argues against an upstream data or cache degradation.
No portfolio-svc get_holdings WARN or ERROR lines were logged, and no portfolio-svc changes were recorded in the window or the roughly 22 hours before it.

assumptions.text: Tokens and orchestrator latency likely moved together, since they both first deviated in the same 10:55 bucket. Per-request token growth, not request volume, is the more likely driver given the flat rps. Neither has been confirmed.
The 400000.0 plateau on tokens_per_min may be a metric ceiling or clamp, not a true measured value. This should be checked before the figure is used for spend estimates.

Roughly 79 'notification sent with empty body' warnings and roughly 90 'template render failed' errors appear in the 200 visible msg-delivery lines (manual count, approximate). About 25 'redelivered 9-10 messages on outbound-msgs' warnings appear in the same window, which suggests failed renders are being redelivered and retried rather than dropped.
The logs carry no user ID or message type, so correlation of blank notifications with specific users, message types or LLM responses cannot be determined from these results.
No config, prompt, model, max-token, retry or rate-limit change appears in the window. This reflects the absence of records, not a verified absence of changes in those systems.
The cluster of events around 10:39 (portfolio-svc cache miss at 10:39:07Z and redis-cache slowlog at 10:39:16Z) is a weak temporal association only, not evidence that redis caused the cache misses.

The zero msg-delivery matches are consistent with H2 (render failures begin after 11:24) and, because the agent loop began at 10:55, they weaken H3's prediction that incomplete payloads would produce render failures from about 10:55.
Zero orchestrator matches for 'portfolio_value' and 'outbound-msgs' may reflect that these payload fields and publishes are not logged at all, not that the publishes were complete.

The 11:24 template refactor is the likely source of the 'portfolio_value' render failures that begin at 11:25:18Z. This rests on timing and the deploy note alone. The diff is not available, so it is unverified whether the refactor made portfolio_value required or whether the orchestrator payload changed.
Only some payloads may lack portfolio_value. Successful renders for other message types would support this, but I did not check logs for them, so it is unverified.

Because the orchestrator loop keeps repeating get_holdings with no portfolio-svc error or empty-data warning logged, the loop is probably generated inside orchestrator and not caused by portfolio-svc failures. This is unverified because the portfolio-svc payloads were not inspected.

A prompt or tool-schema change in orchestrator is not ruled out. get_changes does not track prompt or tool-schema versions, and no orchestrator config record appeared in the window, so this is absence of records rather than a verified absence of change.

actions.text: Roll back msg-delivery-00290 (notification template refactor), or hotfix the template so portfolio_value is optional or has a default.
